pr.title: JumpThreading: compute place and value indices on-demand
pr.description:
Profiling JumpThreading reveals that a large part of the runtime happens constructing the place and value `Map`. This is unfortunate, as jump-threading may end up not even doing anything.

The cause for this large up-front cost is following: `Map` attempts to create a `PlaceIndex` for each place that *may* hold a relevant value. This means all places that appear in MIR, but also all places whose value is accessed by a projection of a copy of a larger place.

This PR refactors the creation of `Map` to happen on-demand: place and value indices are created when threading computation happens.

The up-front mode is still relevant for DataflowConstProp, so is not touched.

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: PR 142881 is an optimization/cost-model refactor of JumpThreading: it replaces eagerly building the place/value `Map` with on-demand registration (`PlaceCollectionMode::OnDemand`), while DataflowConstProp intentionally retains the full eager mode. The frozen analysis itself classifies the eager path as "a performance defect, not a semantic wrong rewrite." The only test artifacts in the patch are coverage `.cov-map` snapshot changes (e.g., `closure#0` becoming unused, `try_error_result::test2` expressions 61→18), which are instrumentation/diagnostic churn, not program-visible numeric/boolean/character results. No regression test or miscompile evidence exists in the historical material. The `register_copy_tree` reordering is a direction-sensitive refactor intended to preserve the same renames mapping; creating an observable value difference would require injecting an unrelated bug (e.g., deliberately reversing key/value insertion), which is not the historical transformation. Therefore no source-grounded original/transformed pair with genuinely different defined Miri values can be constructed without fabricating behavior, so I am not validating a counterexample.

evidence: Profiling JumpThreading reveals that a large part of the runtime happens constructing the place and value `Map`.
This PR refactors the creation of `Map` to happen on-demand: place and value indices are created when threading computation happens.
The up-front mode is still relevant for DataflowConstProp, so is not touched.
let map = Map::new(tcx, body, PlaceCollectionMode::Full { value_limit });
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historical eager transformation (a performance defect, not a semantic wrong rewrite): create place and value indices up front for all syntactic places and all projection descendants propagated from assignments, even when JumpThreading never queries them and even when the function has no threadable condition. The patch replaces this with `PlaceCollectionMode::OnDemand`, where `place and value indices are created when threading computation happens`. This is an optimization PR; it does not establish a miscompilation. DataflowConstProp deliberately keeps eager behavior via `PlaceCollectionMode::Full { value_limit }`, because `The up-front mode is still relevant for DataflowConstProp, so is not touched.`
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies processed by JumpThreading, especially larger bodies with many locals, projections, copies, and aggregate constructions but few or no matching conditions to thread. The same source-level program should produce identical optimized MIR under eager versus on-demand registration; what differs is the amount of unused `Map` construction. Do not apply this as evidence about semantics of DataflowConstProp, which still uses the full eagerly populated map. On-demand inputs must support lazy tail registration for `Discriminant` and `DerefLen`, and lazy scalar-value allocation.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `Map::new` immediately registered all non-excluded locals, collected syntactic places, propagated projections across assignments, created scalar values for every registered place, and trimmed useless places. JumpThreading constructed this map with a fixed limit: `map: Map::new(tcx, body, Some(MAX_PLACES))`, where `const MAX_PLACES: usize = 100;`. The PR description explains the cost: `Profiling JumpThreading reveals that a large part of the runtime happens constructing the place and value Map.` The stated cause is that `Map` `attempts to create a PlaceIndex for each place that may hold a relevant value`, including places accessed through projections of copies of larger places.
pitfalls: Do not use the eager `Full` mode assumptions in on-demand code: `inner_values` may have no cached range, so consuming code must fall back to recursive traversal.

`register_place` with a tail only supports `TrackElem::Discriminant` and `TrackElem::DerefLen`; the patch has `TrackElem::Variant(..) | TrackElem::Field(..) => todo!()`, so variants/fields must be registered through their parent projection index rather than as a tail.

`register_copy_tree` must lazily allocate the target value and recursively recreate matching child projections on the target. Its call in `process_copy` has direction-sensitive renaming: old code used `for_each_value_pair(rhs, lhs, &mut |rhs, lhs| { renames.insert(lhs, rhs); })`; new code calls `register_copy_tree(lhs, rhs, &mut |lhs, rhs| { renames.insert(lhs, rhs); })`. A refactor that swaps key/value insertion changes which conditions survive a copy.
When registering aggregate fields under on-demand mode, the code now passes `operand.ty(self.body, self.tcx)` to `register_place_index` rather than relying on a preexisting projected place.
A prefilter using `values_inside(lhs)` was removed from `process_immediate`; on-demand maps do not have those precomputed ranges.

The patch only updates coverage snapshots such as `tests/coverage/closure.cov-map` and `tests/coverage/try_error_result.cov-map`; these show optimization-output churn (`closure#0` becomes `(unused)` with `Code(Zero)`, and `try_error_result::test2` drops from 61 expressions to 18), but they are not a focused JumpThreading correctness test.
preconditions: JumpThreading must use `PlaceCollectionMode::OnDemand`; DataflowConstProp must continue using `PlaceCollectionMode::Full { value_limit }`.
On-demand registration needs a `typing_env` so `register_value` can normalize the place type and test `layout.backend_repr.is_scalar()` before allocating a value.
Projection tails such as enum discriminants and slice deref lengths must be registered lazily through `register_place(..., tail)` or `register_place_index`.
`create_values`, `trim_useless_places`, and `cache_preorder_invoke` assume the map is fully populated; the patch guards them with `debug_assert_matches!(self.mode, PlaceCollectionMode::Full { .. })`.
`for_each_value_inside` must support both fully cached ranges and on-demand maps by recursing when no cached range exists.
analysis.summary: JumpThreading was refactored from an eagerly prebuilt value-analysis `Map` to on-demand place/value registration (`PlaceCollectionMode::OnDemand`), while DataflowConstProp retains the full eager mode. The reusable lesson is an optimization/cost-model lesson, not a confirmed miscompile: eagerly indexing every syntactic place and propagated projection is wasted when JumpThreading finds no threadable condition.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct paired MIR tests that differ only in whether they exercise queried places. (1) A non-threadable stress body with many locals, copies, and aggregate projections but no matching branch condition: run JumpThreading with eager versus on-demand map behavior and assert the optimized MIR is unchanged while only the on-demand path avoids unused place/value creation. (2) Positive threading cases that require a copy tree, enum discriminant, slice deref length, and aggregate field registration: assert the same threaded branch targets and condition renames as the eager implementation. (3) Exercise a copy where the target already has a value and where the target has no value yet, to verify `register_copy_tree` direction and lazy target allocation. (4) Add a direct MIR regression test rather than relying only on the changed coverage `.cov-map` snapshots. Do not claim execution; no compiler was built for this analysis.
analysis.trigger: JumpThreading is enabled and runs on MIR where constructing the value-analysis map is a significant fraction of pass time, particularly when the pass discovers no threading opportunities. The PR changes `Map::new(tcx, body, Some(MAX_PLACES))` to `Map::new(tcx, body, PlaceCollectionMode::OnDemand)` and removes `MAX_PLACES`, so places and values are materialized only when queried.
